quickAnswer: To generate cryptographically secure UUIDs (Universally Unique Identifiers), select your desired quantity (1 to 100) and choose case, hyphen, and brace formatting. The generator uses browser Web Crypto API randomUUID to provide 122 bits of hardware-backed entropy with zero server communication.

formula.title: RFC 4122 Version 4 UUID Structure
formula.explanation: A Version 4 UUID consists of 128 bits: 4 bits are fixed for the version (0100 for v4), 2 bits specify the variant (10 for RFC 4122), and the remaining 122 bits are filled with cryptographically strong pseudorandom numbers. With 2¹²² possible combinations (approximately 5.3 × 10³⁶), the probability of collision is negligible.

commonMistakes.title: Using Math.random() for UUIDs
commonMistakes.description: Standard JavaScript Math.random() is pseudorandom and predictable. Always require crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues() to prevent identifier collision and forgery.

commonMistakes.title: Treating UUIDs as Secret Passwords
commonMistakes.description: UUIDs are unique identifiers, not authentication tokens or cryptographic keys. They lack cryptographic hashing or salt and should not substitute for secrets.

commonMistakes.title: Assuming Sequential Monotonicity
commonMistakes.description: Version 4 UUIDs are completely random and non-sequential. Using them as clustered database primary keys without sorting indexes can cause B-tree fragmentation.

commonMistakes.title: Case-Sensitive Database Lookups
commonMistakes.description: RFC 4122 specifies that hexadecimal comparisons must be case-insensitive. Failing to normalize case when querying databases can lead to missing records.

faqs.a: A Version 4 UUID is a 128-bit universally unique identifier generated using random numbers. It contains 122 random bits, giving 5.3 × 10³⁶ possible values with virtually zero probability of duplicate generation.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a UUID and a GUID?
faqs.a: GUID (Globally Unique Identifier) is Microsoft's implementation term for UUID (Universally Unique Identifier). In modern software, both refer to identical 128-bit RFC 4122 compliant structures.

faqs.q: How are UUIDs generated securely in this tool?
faqs.a: This tool uses the native browser Web Crypto API (crypto.randomUUID). Entropy is gathered directly from your operating system's cryptographic random hardware generator.

faqs.q: Can two UUID v4 values collide?
faqs.a: While theoretically possible, generating 1 billion UUIDs per second for 100 years yields less than a 50% chance of a single collision. For practical software engineering, UUIDs are universally unique.

faqs.q: Are generated UUIDs transmitted or logged?
faqs.a: Never. Generation executes 100% client-side inside your browser memory. No generated keys or logs ever touch external servers.
